context.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for fraud analysts. It is designed for a mid-size payment processor operating under strict compliance and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway (External source of authorization requests)
- Fraud Analysts (Internal users performing case reviews)
- ML Training Environment (External system for model updates)
- Ingress API Gateway (Traffic shaping and rate limiting)
- Real-Time Scoring Container (Stateless in-memory evaluation engine)
- Case Management Service (Analyst review backend)
- WORM Audit Store (Tamper-evident 7-year audit logging)
- Message Bus (Asynchronous decoupling pipeline)

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to Ingress API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- Ingress API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Container via gRPC
- Real-Time Scoring Container to Message Bus via AWS SQS
- Message Bus to WORM Audit Store via AWS S3 API (Object Lock)
- Analysts to Case Management Service via HTTPS/TLS 1.3

## Technology Stack
- AWS (Primary cloud provider in region eu-west-1)
- AWS ECS Fargate (Provisioned container compute for predictable latency without cold starts)
- AWS S3 Object Lock (Write-Once-Read-Many storage for 7-year tamper-evident audit trails)
- AWS SQS (Asynchronous message bus for decoupling scoring from audit logs)
- In-memory embedded ML runtime (For low-latency model evaluation)

## Rationale
The architecture prioritizes sub-50ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS by using stateless, in-memory containerized scoring and asynchronous decoupling. It satisfies strict PCI-DSS Level 1 and 7-year auditability constraints within a €25,000 monthly budget while remaining maintainable for a three-engineer team.

## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system processes and evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time, while providing case management tools for fraud analysts. It operates in AWS eu-west-1, maintaining sub-50ms P99 latency and strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway (External System)
- AWS API Gateway with Circuit Breaker
- Tokenization Proxy Container
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon SQS Message Bus
- AWS S3 Object Lock (Immutable Audit Storage)
- AWS S3 Glacier (Archival Storage)
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container
- Configuration Validation Init Container

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway to AWS API Gateway via HTTPS/TLS 1.3
- AWS API Gateway to Tokenization Proxy via gRPC/Protobuf
- Tokenization Proxy to Core Scoring Engine via internal VPC network
- Core Scoring Engine to Amazon SQS for asynchronous case routing
- Amazon SQS to Case Management Service via polling
- Core Scoring Engine to AWS S3 Object Lock for tamper-evident audit logging
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar to monitoring backend via OTLP protocol

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS with Fargate: Container orchestration chosen to minimize management toil for a 3-engineer team.
- Modular Monolith: Architecture pattern for the scoring engine to ensure sub-50ms latency and simplify zero-downtime deployments.
- Amazon SQS: Message queue for decoupling real-time scoring from asynchronous analyst case management.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Immutable storage backend to satisfy 7-year tamper-evident audit constraints.
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry: Sidecar telemetry collection for monitoring P99 latency without affecting performance.
- OpenAPI / gRPC: Contract-first API definitions for robust service communication and schema enforcement.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless container orchestration on AWS ECS Fargate and a modular monolith to maximize performance and maintainability within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget and a 3-engineer team constraint. Decoupling asynchronous case management via Amazon SQS and implementing tokenization proxies ensures strict PCI-DSS compliance and sub-50ms P99 decision latency.

AWS API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for fraud analysts. It ensures sub-50ms decision latency at 3,000 transactions per second under strict PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance.

## Key Elements
- Payment Gateway
- AWS API Gateway
- Tokenization Proxy Container
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Case Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Amazon SQS Message Bus
- AWS S3 Object Lock and AWS S3 Glacier
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container
- Configuration Validation Init Container

## Relationships
- Payment Gateway -> AWS API Gateway: Sends payment authorization requests [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- AWS API Gateway -> Tokenization Proxy Container: Forwards payment data [gRPC/Protobuf]
- Tokenization Proxy Container -> Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine: Sends tokenized payloads [gRPC/Protobuf]
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS Message Bus: Queues asynchronous review cases [AMQP/SQS Protocol]
- Case Management Service -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Stores immutable audit logs [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway: Manages external ingress, rate-limiting, and payload size restriction to protect downstream services within budget.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Hosts containerized core scoring and case management engines with minimal operational overhead.
- gRPC and Protobuf: Ensures high-performance, low-latency inter-container communication.
- Amazon SQS: Handles asynchronous message queuing and fallback processing to prevent payment blocking.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident, 7-year auditability for regulatory compliance.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless edge routing and containerized microservices on AWS to achieve high-throughput, low-latency fraud screening within strict budget constraints. Automated infrastructure and lightweight protocols ensure compliance and reliability while remaining maintainable by a three-engineer team.

Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud before approval and provides case management for analysts.

## Key Elements
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Internal Modules: Rule-Evaluation Module, ML-Scoring Module, Fail-Fast Validation Pipeline
* Supporting Infrastructure: AWS API Gateway, Tokenization Proxy Container, Amazon SQS, AWS S3 Object Lock, OpenTelemetry Sidecar

## Relationships
* Tokenization Proxy Container -> Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine: Sends tokenized payment data via internal VPC network
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS: Asynchronously routes review cases via SQS API
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Writes tamper-evident audit logs via AWS SDK

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Provides container orchestration within the 25k EUR budget
* Strategy Pattern & Atomic References: Enables zero-downtime hot-swapping of rules and models in memory
* ArchUnit: Enforces compile-time module boundaries and unidirectional data flow
* OpenTelemetry Sidecar (AWS Distro): Handles asynchronous metric flushing

## Rationale
The modular monolith architecture avoids network hops to meet the <50ms P99 latency target. Thread-safe in-memory hot-swapping and strict resource pooling ensure high throughput while operating within a fixed budget and small team.

Case Management Service.analysis:
## Overview
[The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that screens card-not-present transactions and provides case management tools for fraud analysts. Its core purpose is to evaluate payment authorizations in under 50 ms while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year tamper-evident auditability.]

## Key Elements
- Fraud Analysts
- Case Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate modular monolith)
- Read-Optimized Projection Database (AWS RDS Aurora Serverless v2)
- Event Store and Archival (AWS S3 Object Lock and S3 Glacier)
- Asynchronous Message Broker (Amazon SQS with Dead Letter Queue)
- Observability and Tracing (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry Sidecar)

## Relationships
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Service: Reviews suspicious payments and manages fraud cases [HTTPS/TLS 1.3]
- Case Management Service -> Amazon SQS Message Bus: Consumes case review triggers and asynchronous events [Polling / SQS Protocol]
- Case Management Service -> AWS RDS Aurora Serverless v2: Queries and updates read-optimized case projections [PostgreSQL Protocol / TCP]
- Case Management Service -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Appends immutable domain events and event snapshots [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Hosts the case management modular monolith with minimal operational overhead for a 3-person team.
- AWS RDS Aurora Serverless v2: Provides scalable, lightweight storage for read-optimized CQRS projections within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget.
- AWS S3 Object Lock: Guarantees tamper-evident, immutable 7-year event storage satisfying strict compliance mandates (R-06).
- Amazon SQS & Transactional Outbox: Ensures reliable asynchronous message delivery and prevents split-brain states between services.
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry: Delivers automated synthetic health checks and tracing without dedicated operations staff.

## Rationale
[This architecture combines an event-sourced CQRS modular monolith on AWS ECS Fargate with serverless storage to meet strict compliance, auditability, and performance constraints within budget. The design minimizes operational complexity, ensuring a three-engineer team can reliably maintain the system and scale securely.]

- AWS API Gateway -> Tokenization Proxy Container: Forwards payment payloads [HTTP / JSON]
- Tokenization Proxy Container -> Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine: Sends tokenized data [Internal HTTP / gRPC]
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine -> Amazon SQS Message Bus: Asynchronously offloads audit payloads [AWS SDK / SQS API]
- Amazon SQS Message Bus -> AWS S3 Object Lock: Persists tamper-evident compliance logs [AWS SDK / S3 API]
- AWS S3 Object Lock -> AWS S3 Glacier: Transitions older audit logs via lifecycle policies [S3 Lifecycle]
- Fraud Analysts -> Case Management Service: Reviews suspicious transactions [HTTPS / REST]

## Technology Stack
- AWS ECS Fargate: Runs containerized services without server management to fit the 3-engineer team constraint
- Amazon SQS: Buffers audit logs asynchronously to protect the critical 50 ms payment path
- AWS S3 Object Lock (Compliance Mode): Enforces immutable, tamper-evident 7-year audit retention for PCI-DSS
- AWS S3 Glacier: Reduces long-term storage costs to meet the 25,000 EUR monthly budget
- AWS KMS: Encrypts audit logs with customer-managed keys and automated annual rotation

## Rationale
This architecture decouples non-critical compliance logging from the low-latency payment path using asynchronous SQS buffering. It satisfies strict 7-year immutability and PCI-DSS mandates while maintaining operational simplicity for a three-engineer team within budget.

This system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations and case management for financial fraud analysts. OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container.analysis:
## Overview
The OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container provides lightweight, stateless telemetry collection for the Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system on AWS ECS Fargate. It ensures high-performance observability while protecting system latency and budget constraints.

## Key Elements
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container (AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry)
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
- Monitoring Backend
- AWS SSM Parameter Store

## Relationships
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container -> Monitoring Backend: Exports telemetry and metrics [OTLP over gRPC/HTTP with Gzip compression]
- Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine -> OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container: Sends telemetry and queries queue health [HTTP/gRPC over localhost]
- OpenTelemetry Sidecar Container <- AWS SSM Parameter Store: Retrieves centralized collector configurations [AWS API]

## Technology Stack
- AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry (ADOT): Chosen for standardized, zero-code OpenTelemetry semantic conventions.
- AWS ECS Fargate: Utilized with strict CPU/memory limits and startup dependencies for resource isolation.
- AWS SSM Parameter Store: Selected for centralized, zero-redeploy configuration management.
- Gzip OTLP Compression: Implemented to minimize network bandwidth and cloud egress costs.

## Rationale
This architecture fits the requirements by enforcing stateless sidecar patterns, resource limits, and head-based sampling that protect the strict <50 ms P99 latency threshold. Furthermore, it minimizes operational toil for a three-engineer team while maintaining compliance and staying within the 25k EUR monthly budget.

Configuration Validation Init Container.analysis:
## Overview
The system is a real-time payment fraud screening platform that evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for mid-size processors to prevent fraud before approval. It features an integrated case management dashboard for fraud analysts to review flagged transactions securely and efficiently.

## Key Elements
* Fraud Analysts
* Payment Gateway
* AWS API Gateway (with Circuit Breaker)
* Tokenization Proxy Container
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Case Management Service (AWS ECS Fargate)
* Amazon SQS Message Bus
* AWS S3 Object Lock & AWS S3 Glacier
* Configuration Validation Init Container (Container)
* AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry Sidecar

## Relationships
* Payment Gateway invokes AWS API Gateway using HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for real-time authorization scoring (R-01).
* AWS API Gateway communicates with Tokenization Proxy Container via internal gRPC to tokenize raw card data (R-05).
* Tokenization Proxy Container forwards sanitized requests to Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine via internal gRPC.
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine writes tamper-evident audit logs and model decisions to AWS S3 Object Lock using AWS SDK (R-06).
* Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine enqueues asynchronous review cases to Amazon SQS Message Bus (R-02).
* Case Management Service consumes messages from Amazon SQS via polling for fraud analyst reviews (R-02).
* Configuration Validation Init Container validates read-only mounted configurations on startup using shared schemas before releasing the shared volume marker to the Modular Monolith Core Scoring Engine.

## Technology Stack
* AWS ECS Fargate: Chosen for container orchestration to maintain a fixed infrastructure budget under 25,000 EUR per month.
* Python / Pydantic (or JSON Schema): Utilized within the Configuration Validation Init Container for lightweight, schema-driven validation.
* AWS S3 Object Lock: Implemented for tamper-evident storage to satisfy the 7-year regulatory auditability constraint (R-06).
* AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry: Deployed as a sidecar for distributed tracing and performance monitoring to meet P99 latency targets under 50 ms (R-04).
* gRPC: Selected for low-latency internal container-to-container communication.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless container infrastructure on AWS ECS Fargate to strictly adhere to the 25,000 EUR monthly budget while operating with a lean three-engineer team. Security and compliance controls—such as tokenization proxies, read-only configuration mounts, and immutable S3 storage—ensure full PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and immutable 7-year auditability.
